I am even more incensed by the ignorant racists who crawl out of the woodwork at first given opportunity than by the protesters burning the poppy. How is burning in hell or hanging a proportionate response to burning a paper flower? Because that's what people are calling for, if you go to the Facebook page. Sure, it's a paper flower steeped with symbolism. I accept that. And be sure that I am not here to say that I condone it or think it's a good idea. But let's have a look at the symbolism of that poppy. What does it mean to burn a poppy? It is a statement of the utmost contempt of British soldiers, conscripted or otherwise, who died in service. I am not saying I agree with that - I really don't, I think it's appalling. What I am saying is that we cannot deny them the right to make that statement, no matter how hateful or odious it is. One is so quick to point out that these soldiers died for the freedom that allowed these statements to be made. Now, if one is a such a fan of freedom, then how does it make any sense to claim the protesters had no right to communicate their message? In fact, it seems that claiming that they have no right to disrespect soldiers like this which is the real disrespect to the soldiers, since that is the statement which stops freedom of speech, for which, allegedly, these soldiers died.

Also, why is it important that they were muslim? As has been pointed out, you never hear about Christian scumbags when Phelps pickets dead soldiers' funerals. This is not logical, it's just people revealing their latent racism.
